model.steady_state_copies: retention_days (one per day, deleted after the window)
model.cpu_priced: measured write CPU once per checkpoint plus measured restore CPU once per restore

billing_models.cpu_seconds: only the CPU the process consumed (user+sys) is billed
billing_models.allocated_vcpu_seconds: the wall time the process occupies its vCPU is billed, including fsync waits; this is what a provider that reserves a vCPU charges, and it is the less favourable model for the arm that waits

model.excluded: fixture hashing, fixture verification and process start-up are outside the priced CPU, exactly as the contract excludes them from the measured phases
model.what_this_is_not: not a forecast, not an economic claim, no fleet, no utilisation, no discount, no reserved-instance, no egress and no request price

unpriced.why: the with/without measurement is a POSIX court, so its 'requests' are file operations, not billable HTTP requests; pricing them at a per-1,000-request object-store rate would compare different units

the measured wall time is a single process on 4 shared vCPUs; a wall second is not a billable unit and no $/second is claimed. CPU seconds are the priced proxy, and they are measured separately in the same receipt.
the with/without measurement is local; no egress or transfer quantity was measured, so none is priced
no memory-reservation price is cited; the difference is reported as a resource quantity only

cannot_prove: the rows come from four different courts and three different fixtures (Qwen2.5-0.5B with 8 shards, a small CPU-only Python transformer, a synthetic reuse trace); they are not one end-to-end run and their sum is not a measured end-to-end cost
the write rows measure a single checkpoint, not a training schedule; the async and resume rows measure a different, much smaller model
the retention rows are a synthetic deterministic reuse trace, not a serving workload; they order the same reachability-safe set and say nothing about a real hit-rate
no row measures a GPU, a fleet, a network, or media failure
the partial-restore rows are layers of one transformer block on CPU; the receipt itself says a whole-model next step needs every tensor
the break-even surface assumes one checkpoint per day, steady-state retention, one restore per checkpoint by default, and prices that do not change with volume or commitment
